# `scope_set_eq_mode`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Switch the mount between equatorial and alt-azimuth operation.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0x7cff0 (64-bit build); driver SetEqMode @0xf2900 (status read, "not home pos" branch sets 254), SetEqModeCmd @0xf0aa0 (mode command, LoadUserLocation, location re-apply, MountMode emit) |

Needs a connected mount (315) and a valid equ_mode (106). The driver mode setter reads the controller status and requires the mount to be at its home (folded) position; otherwise it fails with 254 and sends nothing (INFERRED that the status flag tested means "at home"). It then sends the controller's equatorial or alt-azimuth mode command; a failed write replies with the thread error code, no specific code being set. After a successful write it reloads the stored user location and re-applies it to the mount for the new mode (failures there are only logged), emits MountMode with equ_mode, and the handler replies 0. A client SHOULD park first, or use scope_park with equ_mode. Served by the guider process (TCP 4400); a client on the main command port reaches it through the imager unknown-method relay, which is unavailable to guest-table clients. The native-handler grade below does not describe the relay. Mount serial (firmware 9.31, READ): requires the home flag H in :GU, then :AA (alt-az) or :AP (equatorial).

Side effects: Changes the mount mode and re-applies the stored site location to the mount. MountMode with equ_mode is emitted only after a successful mode write (READ; see mount-and-motion R40).

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |
| 106 | equ_mode missing, null or not a boolean/integer | `expected bool param` |
| 315 | No mount is connected | `mount is not connected` |
| 254 | The mount is not at its home (folded) position; nothing is sent | `mount operation failed` |

A failed mode write replies with the current thread error code, which the driver does not set to a specific value; those codes are not exhausted by this table.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":51,"method":"scope_set_eq_mode","params":{"equ_mode":true}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_set_eq_mode","result":0,"code":0,"id":51}
```

Reply, err-106:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_set_eq_mode","error":"expected bool param","code":106,"id":52}
```

Reply, not-home - Mount not at its home position:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_set_eq_mode","error":"mount operation failed","code":254,"id":53}
```
